units.text: Let's pick the tool by the evidence we need. Use CloudTrail for recorded A P I activity and Config for the resource's configuration history. Inspector helps identify software exposure, GuardDuty reports threat signals, and Macie helps find sensitive S three data. The tools answer different questions.

Use Detective when the investigation needs relationships and timelines around a finding. A security finding can guide the investigation; it does not replace the original records or prove the whole story.

Start with the finding and identify its account, Region, resource and time. Look up the relevant A P I, flow or configuration evidence for that same scope. The finding says where to look; the records help establish what actually happened.

In this example, compare the recorded A P I activity and available network context with expected use. Assign the result to an owner and decide whether monitoring, investigation or an approved corrective action is justified.
Use Artifact when an auditor needs an A W S assurance report, such as the SOC report shown here. It describes controls managed by A W S; it does not cover the workload evidence you must supply.

Audit Manager can collect workload evidence for eligible existing deployments. A W S no longer permits new account setups, and existing use has scope limits. For resource compliance monitoring without an eligible deployment, evaluate Config conformance packs. Evidence collection doesn't award certification.

A residency rule follows the data, not just its primary bucket. Check replication, backups, logs, analytical exports and support handling against approved locations. Map what actually moves and where it lands.

Use supported organization, resource and application controls according to the boundary. A regional encryption key alone doesn't guarantee residency. Verify the controls against the complete data and metadata paths.

We'll review how a generative AI workflow gets from input to an action. A content filter may catch policy violations, but it can miss issues. Keep enough redacted evidence for an authorized review without recording sensitive prompts or responses indiscriminately.

A high-impact action can wait for a human decision. Give the reviewer the proposed action and context, then follow the approved or rejected branch. Verify that rejected actions cannot continue to execution.

Workload accounts collect signals where their resources run. A delegated security account can centralize the supported findings and investigation context. Check coverage in each account and Region before interpreting the centralized view.

Use a scoped central workflow to route work to the right owner. A high-impact response needs authorization before a change. Verify at the originating resource; a central finding status alone doesn't prove remediation.
We'll verify a fix from evidence, not from a green automation status. Config records the bucket change and the rule evaluates it as noncompliant. The runbook then applies the scoped correction.

Check that the relevant setting is now correct and that the rule reevaluated it. Review the remaining access policy before declaring exposure resolved. A setting can be noncompliant without proving any unauthorized access occurred.

Associate the Inspector finding with the affected image digest. Update the dependency and rebuild, then deploy the corrected image. Verify the workload runs the new digest and the relevant scan no longer reports the issue for that deployed artifact.

Start from the unusual credential finding, then check relevant activity and timing in Detective and CloudTrail. Ask the responsible owner whether the activity matches approved work. An anomaly alone is not proof that the account was compromised.

If evidence confirms a problem, use your approved containment process for the affected identity and verify the result. Keep the incident evidence. Don't disable unrelated accounts just because one finding looks suspicious.
Macie can report sensitive content and a separate bucket concern. Validate both: which object is affected, and what access is actually allowed? The first fact does not establish the second.

After approval, apply the smallest appropriate change to the access or data boundary and test it. Confirm the unintended access is gone, required access still works, and record the result without copying the sensitive values.

We'll choose a managed AI service by what goes in and what should come out. For images, Rekognition can return visual analysis. Textract focuses on document content, and Transcribe converts speech to text. Start with the desired result rather than assuming one model fits every input.

Rekognition analyzes supported images or video to return task-specific results, such as labels or moderation signals. It doesn't decide whether an application should act. Set an appropriate decision policy and validate the output on your own examples.

For an image you may want detected objects or recognized text; for video you might track items over time. A face similarity score is not proof of identity. Check suitability and enforce the application's consent and review policy.

A lower minimum confidence returns more labels and can create more false positives. A higher threshold can omit relevant labels. Define which borderline results need human review. A2I is a legacy option for eligible existing customers; plan a suitable review workflow for a new design.
